title: London forecast (Open-Meteo)
what: Forecast for London from Open-Meteo: hourly temperature, chance and amount of rain, wind and weather code for 3 days, each day's lowest and highest temperature, and every forecast we served kept for 14 days. A model forecast for a grid point, not a warning.

schedule.how: the Pages workflow (.github/workflows/pages.yml) at 17 minutes past 00, 06, 12 and 18 UTC; one request a run (four a day, far under the 10,000 a day of the free API); every other run keeps the last read, copied from the live site

terms.summary: Used under Open-Meteo's free non-commercial terms because data.promptugal.news is free and carries no subscriptions or adverts (Dinis, 18 Nov 2026). Sites that charge must not reuse it without a paid plan; that line is still being settled. Data CC BY 4.0: credit Open-Meteo (link to https://open-meteo.com/) and the models' providers, and say if changed. Not reviewed by a person.
terms.quote: You may only use the free API services for non-commercial purposes. [...] Private or non-profit websites or apps that do not have subscriptions or advertising. [...] the following examples are considered commercial use: Websites or apps that have subscriptions or display advertisements.
terms.republish: yes under CC BY 4.0 with attribution; the free API is for non-commercial use only, so a reuser who charges needs a paid plan
terms.open_question: Dinis's decision (board/team/data/briefs/2026-11-18-dinis-europe-open-data-public-service.md) is that this site is non-commercial; if it ever takes subscriptions or adverts this source must move to a paid plan or the Met Office DataHub. security@PrompTugal.dinis to review.

code: the collector reads Open-Meteo's forecast API for the point on the card, names the fields, and carries earlier forecasts into history
GitHub Actions runs it and deploys the site
agents: data.b.dev@PrompTugal.dinis wrote the collector and card on 18 November 2026 for data.b@ (WS-177)
people: Dinis Cruz decided London as the first place beyond Portugal (board/guidance/2026-11-18-london.md) and the use of the free non-commercial API (18 November 2026, about 22:40 UTC); no person has checked the values (not reviewed)

cost.runner: GitHub Actions on a public repository: no charge; one request a run (about 4 KB)
cost.note: Code only: no model is called when the data is collected.
